## Motivation

Add SM100 NVFP4 KV cache support for GLM-5.2 DSA. Allow the existing layer-split flag to store target KV layers on their owning interleave-CP ranks. Support PD prefill and unified prefill/decode serving with EAGLE/MTP.

This is a draft. Local correctness checks and a long-context capacity run are complete. Dataset accuracy and a controlled, repeated throughput/latency comparison remain open.

## Modifications

- Add the SM100 FlashMLA NVFP4 specialization and DSA codec. Main-cache rows use 416 packed bytes. The indexer uses 132 bytes per row.
- Initialize per-layer FP32 global scales in the shared MLA pool path. Preserve scale values and addresses when buffers are rebuilt. Return raw packed bytes from layer-split getters.
- Support NVFP4 with interleave CP and PD prefill layer splitting. Preserve layer mapping, byte widths, and full draft caches.
- Add unified serving with TP=CP>1, DP=1, and PP=1. Prefill transfers the active physical pages, including cached prefixes. Layer owners compute decode/target-verification attention and broadcast the results. Decode and target verification support CUDA Graphs.
- Account for local layers, remote scratch, indexer buffers, scales, and prefill staging. Use 64-bit cache address arithmetic. Assemble paged DSA logits one chunk at a time to reduce peak allocation.
- Add regression tests, benchmark drivers, and launch examples. Reuse the existing CLI flags. The NVFP4 path requires page size 64, `flashmla_sparse` prefill, and `flashmla_kv` decode. PD layer splitting still requires Mooncake.

## Accuracy Tests

Validation uses commit `9221ec3618b2aba7390711982a766312c9f2e858`.

- 97 test cases passed across the first 11 local validation stages. Coverage includes CP=2/4, nonuniform layer ownership and scales, packed-byte cache operations, prefetch/write behavior, prefix/chunked prefill, owner routing and CUDA Graphs, large index-cache offsets, and FP8 regression.
- The initial paged-logit validator failed on exact top-k index equality at tied boundary scores. A follow-up GPU regression passed all 6 cases in eager execution and two CUDA Graph replays. Valid logits are exactly equal (`rtol=0, atol=0`). Different selected indices occur only at exactly equal boundary scores; selected score multisets match full `torch.topk`. Numerical tolerances were not widened.
- The unified long-context run completed all 1,280 requests with zero retractions. This checks request completion, not model accuracy.
- Dataset accuracy has **not** been evaluated. A full GSM8K test and acceptance runner are included but are not reported as passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Local paged-logit regression collected 84 timing samples. For the large draft case (batch 512), peak temporary allocation fell from 10.56 GiB to 5.54 GiB; median GPU time rose by 1.3%. For native target verification at batch 512, allocation fell from 10.55 GiB to 6.84 GiB; median GPU time fell by 3.45%. These results apply only to those local cases.

The full-model capacity run used 8 GB300 GPUs in one NVLink domain, unified TP=CP=8, DP=1, NVFP4 KV, and EAGLE steps=5/topk=1/draft tokens=6. The KV allocation ceiling was 152 GiB per GPU, including target, indexer, remote scratch, complete draft cache, scales, and staging. The workload used 640 two-turn sessions, about 64K mean input tokens, up to 450,560 input tokens, and about 400 mean output tokens.

| Metric | Layer split ON, client concurrency 256 |
| --- | ---: |
| Successful requests | 1,280 / 1,280 |
| Output throughput | 405.03 tokens/s |
| TTFT p50 / p95 | 4.77 / 175.53 s |
| TPOT p50 / p95 | 643.69 / 4,257.78 ms |
| Mean running requests, middle 20–80% window | 251.02 |
| Mean / peak active KV occupancy | 56.91% / 64.66% |

All ranks stayed within the KV allocation ceiling. Uneven layer ownership leaves different per-rank allocations. Six CUDA allocator allocation-failure/retry warnings occurred; the run then completed all requests.

Historical OFF results at the same per-GPU KV ceiling reached 392.19 tokens/s at concurrency 64 and 315.36 tokens/s at concurrency 128, with lower tail latency. Those runs used different physical GPUs, source revisions, and request manifests. They are not a controlled comparison. This single ON run does not establish a repeatable throughput/latency benefit, and active KV capacity was not saturated.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -85,11 +85,17 @@ Prefill CP can coexist with supported speculative-decoding configurations. The C
 
 The shared CP breakable-prefill-graph path currently requires `zigzag`, the `trtllm_mha` prefill backend, PP=1, and attention CP size equal to TP size. It uses CP-local static input buffers and selects capture buckets large enough for each rank's padded input. Support for combining other attention backends with prefill CP and Breakable CUDA Graph is under development.
 
-### Prefill CP × PD disaggregation and DSA cache LayerSplit
+### Prefill CP × DSA cache LayerSplit
 
 In supported DSA deployments, `--enable-dsa-cache-layer-split` distributes GPU KV/indexer cache layers across CP ranks to reduce per-rank cache memory. Each rank owns a range of layers and uses scratch storage for remote-layer data. This is layer-wise cache ownership, separate from the interleave token assignment used for computation, and is not applied to draft workers.
 
-LayerSplit requires a PD prefill worker (`--disaggregation-mode prefill`), `--enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave`, and PP=1. It currently supports the `mooncake` and `mooncake_tcp` transfer backends. Do not enable LayerSplit on decode or non-PD workers; the decode side receives full cache shards through PD transfer. Use the [PD disaggregation guide](https://docs.sglang.io/docs/advanced_features/pd_disaggregation) and model-specific launch recipes to configure both sides of the transfer; enabling prefill CP alone does not configure a PD deployment.
+In PD mode, LayerSplit requires a prefill worker (`--disaggregation-mode prefill`), `--enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave`, and PP=1. It supports the `mooncake` and `mooncake_tcp` transfer backends. Do not enable LayerSplit on a PD decode worker; that worker receives full cache shards through PD transfer. Use the [PD disaggregation guide](/docs/advanced_features/pd_disaggregation) and model-specific launch recipes to configure both sides. Existing PD FP8 configurations keep their model and backend requirements. The [PD NVFP4 recipe](/docs/advanced_features/quantized_kv_cache#pd-layer-splitting-with-nvfp4) uses the GLM-5.2 FlashMLA path.
+
+Unified serving (`--disaggregation-mode null`) also supports LayerSplit for GLM-5.2 DSA with NVFP4 KV on SM100. It requires TP=CP greater than one, DP=1, attention DP=1, DCP=1, PP=1, interleave prefill CP, 64-token pages, and unpooled index keys. Use `flashmla_sparse` for prefill and `flashmla_kv` for decode. Unified FP8 LayerSplit, CP decode attention TP, and two-batch overlap are not supported. EAGLE/MTP draft workers retain their complete cache.
+
+In this unified mode, eager CP prefill transfers the full batch's required physical pages into remote scratch. Decode and target verification run each layer's attention on its cache owner. See the [eight-GPU launch example](/docs/advanced_features/quantized_kv_cache#unified-serving-with-nvfp4-layer-splitting).
+
+To compare capacity, use the same per-GPU KV byte budget for ON and OFF. Include remote scratch, global scales, the complete draft pool, both prefill staging buffers, and page-ID storage. Choose token capacity separately for each mode. Sweep client concurrency independently so ON can use its additional capacity. Record actual running requests and active KV occupancy, then compare throughput at the same latency limit. See the [comparison procedure](/docs/advanced_features/quantized_kv_cache#compare-on-and-off-with-the-same-kv-byte-budget). Prefill CP alone does not shard cache storage, and LayerSplit does not guarantee a throughput improvement.
 
 ## Usage and Examples

@@ -95,6 +95,285 @@ python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
 Native NVFP4 prefill requires SM100, a page size divisible by 4, and an attention head dimension divisible by 64. TRT-LLM GenMHA uses FP8 query and output buffers internally; SGLang converts the result back to the model activation dtype. Top-k-1 EAGLE/EAGLE3/NEXTN and breadth-1 NGRAM speculative decoding are supported: an EAGLE-family draft worker uses `trtllm_mha`, and target verification consumes the physical NVFP4 cache directly in eager execution and CUDA Graphs. Set `--speculative-ngram-max-bfs-breadth=1` for NGRAM. With the mixed FlashInfer-prefill/TRT-LLM-decode recipe, SGLang resolves `--speculative-attention-mode` to `decode` so verification does not depend on FlashInfer's transient dequantization workspace. Other speculative algorithms, PD disaggregation, hierarchical KV cache, and LMCache are not currently supported by the SM100 native NVFP4 path. SM120 XQA continues to use its architecture-specific linear scale layout and BF16 query/output path.
 </Note>
 
+### GLM-5.2 DSA NVFP4 on SM100
+
+SGLang has a fused NVFP4 KV-cache decode path for the GLM-5.2 DSA layout on
+NVIDIA SM100 GPUs. The implementation stores each main-cache token in 416
+bytes: 256 bytes of packed E2M1 latent values, 32 bytes of block-16 E4M3
+scales, and 128 bytes of BF16 RoPE values. Together with the 132-byte DSA
+indexer row, this uses 548 bytes per token per layer.
+
+The specialization requires the GLM-5.2 DSA shape (512 NoPE dimensions, 64
+RoPE dimensions, and 512 value dimensions), 64 local query heads, and a page
+size of 64. Attention DP provides this head count in the following TP8 launch:
+
+```bash Command
+export MODEL_PATH="${MODEL_PATH:?set MODEL_PATH to the GLM-5.2 checkpoint}"
+
+python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
+    --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" \
+    --tp-size 8 \
+    --dp-size 8 \
+    --enable-dp-attention \
+    --attention-backend dsa \
+    --dsa-prefill-backend flashmla_sparse \
+    --dsa-decode-backend flashmla_kv \
+    --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 \
+    --page-size 64
+```
+
+The weight dtype and weight-quantization method are independent of the KV
+cache format and should be selected for the checkpoint being served. Decode
+reads the packed cache directly and performs E2M1 dequantization inside the
+FlashMLA producer before the existing BF16 attention consumer. It does not
+materialize a full BF16 cache. Prefill gathers and dequantizes the paged prefix
+into a BF16 compatibility workspace for FlashMLA sparse-prefill; only decode is
+fused, and ordinary decode supports CUDA Graph replay.
+
+Prefill context parallelism is supported with the CP-v2 interleave strategy.
+Each CP rank first all-gathers the BF16 latent K/RoPE rows into logical token
+order. By default, each rank writes a replicated NVFP4 cache. CP alone does not
+shard KV-cache capacity or reduce the BF16 CP communication volume. For TP8, use:
+
+```bash Command
+python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
+    --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" \
+    --tp-size 8 \
+    --dp-size 1 \
+    --enable-prefill-cp \
+    --cp-strategy interleave \
+    --attn-cp-size 8 \
+    --attention-backend dsa \
+    --dsa-prefill-backend flashmla_sparse \
+    --dsa-decode-backend flashmla_kv \
+    --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 \
+    --page-size 64
+```
+
+Prefill CUDA Graph is disabled while Prefill CP is active; ordinary decode
+CUDA Graph remains available.
+
+This path currently rejects non-SM100 devices, other DSA model layouts, local
+query-head counts other than 64, page sizes other than 64, DCP, non-interleave
+Prefill CP, and Prefill CP decode attention-TP.
+HiSparse is not supported on this path. The native FlashMLA operator must be
+rebuilt from a source revision that includes the SM100 NVFP4 specialization; a
+missing operator is reported at backend initialization instead of silently
+falling back to an unfused decode path.
+
+#### Unified serving with NVFP4 layer splitting
+
+You can also enable `--enable-dsa-cache-layer-split` on one server that handles
+both prefill and decode (`--disaggregation-mode null`). This mode requires:
+
+- A GLM-5.2 DSA checkpoint with the SM100 layout described above.
+- `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4` and `--page-size 64`.
+- Interleave prefill CP, with TP=CP greater than one.
+- DP=1, attention DP=1, DCP=1, and PP=1.
+- `flashmla_sparse` prefill and `flashmla_kv` decode.
+- Unpooled index keys (`index_kpool=1` in the model configuration).
+
+Unified layer splitting does not support FP8 KV, CP decode attention TP, or
+two-batch overlap. Prefill runs eagerly. Decode and EAGLE target verification
+can use CUDA Graphs. EAGLE/MTP draft workers keep their complete cache.
+
+The target pool stores only the layers owned by each CP rank. During eager
+CP prefill, it transfers the physical cache pages needed by the full batch,
+including cached prefixes. A shared prefix page is transferred once per layer.
+The remote scratch buffers retain their full capacity. During decode and target
+verification, each layer owner computes attention and broadcasts its result.
+These transfers add work; measure their effect on your workload.
+
+The following example uses one Linux host with eight NVIDIA SM100 GPUs. Use a
+GLM-5.2 checkpoint that includes the native MTP weights. Set `KV_TOKEN_CAPACITY`
+to a multiple of 64 that fits your per-GPU KV budget. The next section explains
+how to choose separate capacities for layer splitting ON and OFF.
+Use an SGLang source revision with unified NVFP4 layer splitting and a matching
+`sgl-kernel` build with the SM100 FlashMLA NVFP4 operator.
+
+```bash Unified NVFP4 layer split
+export MODEL_PATH="/path/to/GLM-5.2-checkpoint"
+export KV_TOKEN_CAPACITY="${KV_TOKEN_CAPACITY:?set the budgeted KV token capacity}"
+
+python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
+    --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" \
+    --trust-remote-code \
+    --disaggregation-mode null \
+    --tp-size 8 --dp-size 1 --attn-dp-size 1 \
+    --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave --attn-cp-size 8 \
+    --enable-dsa-cache-layer-split \
+    --attention-backend dsa --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 --page-size 64 \
+    --dsa-prefill-backend flashmla_sparse --dsa-decode-backend flashmla_kv \
+    --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --max-prefill-tokens 16384 \
+    --max-total-tokens "$KV_TOKEN_CAPACITY" --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
+    --max-running-requests 1024 \
+    --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled --cuda-graph-backend-decode full \
+    --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 256 \
+    --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 5 \
+    --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6
+```
+
+The checkpoint's weight format does not select the KV format. Keep
+`--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4` explicit. This unified configuration uses the same
+server endpoint for both phases and does not need a PD router.
+
+#### Compare ON and OFF with the same KV byte budget
+
+Use the same hardware, source revision, checkpoint, calibration, attention
+backends, and EAGLE settings. Keep prefill CP enabled in both configurations.
+For OFF, remove only `--enable-dsa-cache-layer-split` from the feature settings.
+Choose the KV token capacity and client concurrency separately for each mode.
+
+1. Set one KV allocation ceiling in bytes for each GPU. Include target KV and
+   indexer buffers, remote scratch, all global scales, and the complete draft
+   pool. Also include `prefill_main_staging_bytes`,
+   `prefill_index_staging_bytes`, and `prefill_page_ids_bytes` for ON.
+2. Select the largest page-aligned `--max-total-tokens` that stays within that
+   ceiling on every rank. Check the startup `DSA NVFP4 pool bytes` JSON records.
+   Sum `total_bytes` for the target and draft pools on each GPU. Layer ownership
+   can be uneven, so check every rank. The same `--mem-fraction-static` value
+   alone does not establish an equal KV byte budget.
+3. Keep the long-context request set, input/output lengths, prefix reuse,
+   context limit, scheduler limits, and graph settings fixed. Sweep client
+   concurrency independently. ON can use a higher client concurrency to use
+   its additional token capacity. Increase concurrency until the KV budget is
+   used or the agreed latency limit is reached.
+4. Record actual running requests, waiting requests, active KV occupancy,
+   prefix-cache hits, and retractions. Client concurrency includes queued work;
+   it does not measure the number of resident requests.
+5. Compare completed-request throughput against TTFT, TPOT, and end-to-end
+   latency at the same latency limit. Save errors, timeouts, run duration,
+   launch commands, allocation records, and versions. Repeat candidate points
+   before reporting a throughput or latency improvement.
+
+For token capacity `T` and page size 64, ON allocates `T / 64 + 1` page-ID
+entries, including the reserved page. Its two staging buffers each hold at most
+`min(1024, T / 64 + 1)` pages. Their combined size is
+`min(1024, T / 64 + 1) * 64 * (416 + 132)` bytes. Page IDs use another
+`(T / 64 + 1) * 8` bytes. The 416-byte main row is already packed; do not halve
+it again for FP4. Keep these buffers separate from the full-capacity remote
+scratch buffers when calculating the budget.
+
+An equal-concurrency test measures the transfer cost at that offered load.
+The independent concurrency sweeps also test whether the extra capacity changes
+throughput at an acceptable latency. Neither test guarantees an improvement.
+
+#### PD layer splitting with NVFP4
+
+On NVIDIA SM100, `--enable-dsa-cache-layer-split` can shard the NVFP4 main cache
+and the DSA indexer cache across the Prefill CP ranks. Each rank stores its owned
+layers and one remote-layer scratch buffer. Per-layer FP32 global scales remain
+replicated. The main cache uses 416 bytes per token per stored layer. The indexer
+uses 132 bytes per token per stored layer. Include both scratch buffers when
+measuring memory savings.
+
+In PD mode, layer splitting requires a Prefill worker, interleave CP, Mooncake transfer,
+and PP=1. The Decode worker receives the complete cache and uses attention DP.
+EAGLE/MTP draft workers retain their complete cache. Use the same checkpoint and
+per-layer scale calibration on both sides. The model's weight format does not
+select the KV cache format; set `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4` explicitly on both sides.
+
+The following Linux/CUDA example targets one eight-GPU B300 node. Set
+`MODEL_PATH` to a GLM-5.2 checkpoint in both terminals. Start Prefill on GPUs 0–3:
+
+```bash Prefill
+python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
+    --model-path "${MODEL_PATH:?set MODEL_PATH to the GLM-5.2 checkpoint}" \
+    --port 30001 --nccl-port 29501 \
+    --disaggregation-mode prefill \
+    --disaggregation-bootstrap-port 8998 \
+    --disaggregation-transfer-backend mooncake \
+    --tp-size 4 --dp-size 1 --base-gpu-id 0 \
+    --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave --attn-cp-size 4 \
+    --enable-dsa-cache-layer-split \
+    --attention-backend dsa --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 --page-size 64 \
+    --dsa-prefill-backend flashmla_sparse --dsa-decode-backend flashmla_kv \
+    --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --max-prefill-tokens 4096 \
+    --max-total-tokens 131072 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
+    --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 5 \
+    --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6
+```
+
+Start Decode on GPUs 4–7:
+
+```bash Decode

+                CONTEXT_LENGTH, generator=generator, device=device, dtype=torch.int64
+            )[:TOPK].to(torch.int32)
+            indices[request, query] = row + request_start

+    boundary_values = torch.tensor(

+            63,
+            64,
+            65,
+            2047,
+            2048,
+            199_999,
+            200_000,
+            200_001,
+            201_999,
+            202_000,
+        ],
+        dtype=torch.int32,
+        device=device,
+    )
+    indices[0, 0, : boundary_values.numel()] = boundary_values
+    indices[0, 0, 20] = -1
+    indices[0, 0, 21] = indices[0, 0, 22]

+    topk_length[-1] = TOPK - 1

+    valid_locations = torch.unique(
+        indices[(indices >= 0) & (indices < physical_tokens)].to(torch.int64)
+    )
+    latent = (
+        torch.randn(
+            valid_locations.numel(),
+            1,
+            V_DIM,
+            generator=generator,
+            dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+            device=device,
+        )
+        * 0.125

+    rope = (
+        torch.randn(

+    return q, cache, global_scale, indices, topk_length, sink
+

+"""GLM-5.2 DSA mixed NVFP4/BF16 key-cache codec.
+
+The SM100 cache row is intentionally byte-addressed and has one canonical
+layout per physical token::
+
+    [ E2M1 latent (256 B) | E4M3 block-16 scales (32 B) | BF16 RoPE (128 B) ]
+
+Only the 512-dimensional latent vector uses NVFP4 block scaling.  The
+64-dimensional RoPE vector is stored directly as BF16.  The fused attention
+producer dequantizes the latent vector to BF16 and feeds the unchanged
+FlashMLA FP8-cache BF16 QK/PV consumer.  A persistent FP32 global scale is
+stored once per layer by the KV pool, outside this row.
+
+The PyTorch functions are executable, bit-exact references.  The Triton path
+scatters directly into the cache and is used for production cache writes; it
+does not materialize a full-cache dequantization workspace.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import math
+from numbers import Real
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+NVFP4_BLOCK_SIZE = 16
+NVFP4_LATENT_DIM = 512
+NVFP4_ROPE_DIM = 64
+NVFP4_PACKED_LATENT_BYTES = 256
+NVFP4_SCALE_BYTES = 32
+NVFP4_ROPE_BYTES = 128
+NVFP4_BYTES_PER_TOKEN = 416
+
+_E2M1_MAX = 6.0
+_E4M3_MAX = 448.0
+_NUM_LATENT_BLOCKS = NVFP4_LATENT_DIM // NVFP4_BLOCK_SIZE
+_QUANTIZE_SMALL_BATCH_THRESHOLD = 64
+
+
+def _as_feature_matrix(x: torch.Tensor, dim: int, name: str) -> torch.Tensor:
+    if x.ndim == 3 and x.shape[1] == 1:
+        x = x[:, 0, :]
+    if x.ndim != 2 or x.shape[1] != dim:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{name} must have shape [num_tokens, {dim}] or "
+            f"[num_tokens, 1, {dim}], got {tuple(x.shape)}"
+        )
+    if x.dtype not in (torch.bfloat16, torch.float16, torch.float32):
+        raise TypeError(f"{name} must be BF16, FP16, or FP32, got {x.dtype}")
+    return x if x.stride(1) == 1 else x.contiguous()
+
+
+def _as_cache_rows(kv_buffer: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    if kv_buffer.dtype != torch.uint8:
+        raise TypeError(f"kv_buffer must be uint8, got {kv_buffer.dtype}")
+    if kv_buffer.ndim < 2 or kv_buffer.shape[-1] != NVFP4_BYTES_PER_TOKEN:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"kv_buffer must have shape [..., {NVFP4_BYTES_PER_TOKEN}], "
+            f"got {tuple(kv_buffer.shape)}"
+        )
+    if not kv_buffer.is_contiguous():
+        raise ValueError("kv_buffer must be contiguous")
+    return kv_buffer.view(-1, NVFP4_BYTES_PER_TOKEN)
+
+
+def _as_global_scale(
+    global_scale: torch.Tensor | Real, device: torch.device
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    if isinstance(global_scale, torch.Tensor):
+        if global_scale.numel() != 1:
+            raise ValueError("global_scale must contain exactly one value")
+        scale = global_scale.to(device=device, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(1)
+        if not scale.is_cuda and not bool(
+            torch.isfinite(scale).all() & (scale > 0).all()
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("global_scale must be finite and positive")
+        return scale.contiguous()
+    if not isinstance(global_scale, Real):
+        raise TypeError("global_scale must be a number or one-element tensor")
+    value = float(global_scale)
+    if not math.isfinite(value) or value <= 0:
+        raise ValueError(f"global_scale must be finite and positive, got {value}")
+    return torch.tensor([value], dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+
+
+def _validate_quant_inputs(
+    k_nope: torch.Tensor,
+    k_rope: torch.Tensor,
+    kv_buffer: torch.Tensor,
+    loc: torch.Tensor,
+):
+    k_nope = _as_feature_matrix(k_nope, NVFP4_LATENT_DIM, "k_nope")
+    k_rope = _as_feature_matrix(k_rope, NVFP4_ROPE_DIM, "k_rope")
+    rows = _as_cache_rows(kv_buffer)
+    loc = loc.reshape(-1)
+    if k_nope.shape[0] != k_rope.shape[0] or k_nope.shape[0] != loc.numel():
+        raise ValueError("k_nope, k_rope, and loc must have the same token count")
+    if loc.dtype not in (torch.int32, torch.int64):
+        raise TypeError(f"loc must be int32 or int64, got {loc.dtype}")
+    if not (k_nope.device == k_rope.device == rows.device == loc.device):
+        raise ValueError("all codec tensors must be on one device")
+    return k_nope, k_rope, rows, loc.contiguous()
+
+
+def _sanitize_nonfinite_torch(x: torch.Tensor, global_scale: torch.Tensor):
+    """Canonical finite-only policy for E2M1FN/E4M3FN storage.
+
+    NaN becomes positive zero.  Positive/negative infinity saturates to the
+    largest value representable by the recipe at the current global scale.
+    This policy is deterministic in both the CPU reference and CUDA writer.
+    """
+
+    bound = _E2M1_MAX * _E4M3_MAX * global_scale
+    return torch.nan_to_num(
+        x, nan=0.0, posinf=float("inf"), neginf=float("-inf")
+    ).clamp(min=-bound, max=bound)
+
+
+def _e2m1_rne_scaled_torch(x: torch.Tensor, denominator: torch.Tensor):
+    """Encode x/denominator using midpoint comparisons, without reciprocal.
+
+    Strict/non-strict comparisons alternate at the seven E2M1 midpoints to
+    implement round-to-nearest-even exactly.  Reciprocal multiplication is not
+    equivalent at exact ties because it can move the value by one FP32 ULP.
+    """
+
+    magnitude = x.abs()
+    code = (
+        (magnitude > denominator * 0.25).to(torch.uint8)
+        + (magnitude >= denominator * 0.75).to(torch.uint8)
+        + (magnitude > denominator * 1.25).to(torch.uint8)
+        + (magnitude >= denominator * 1.75).to(torch.uint8)
+        + (magnitude > denominator * 2.5).to(torch.uint8)
+        + (magnitude >= denominator * 3.5).to(torch.uint8)
+        + (magnitude > denominator * 5.0).to(torch.uint8)
+    )
+    code |= torch.signbit(x).to(torch.uint8) << 3
+    return torch.where(denominator > 0, code, torch.zeros_like(code))
+
+
+def _decode_e2m1_torch(code: torch.Tensor):
+    lut = torch.tensor(
+        [
+            0.0,
+            0.5,
+            1.0,
+            1.5,
+            2.0,
+            3.0,
+            4.0,
+            6.0,
+            -0.0,
+            -0.5,
+            -1.0,
+            -1.5,
+            -2.0,
+            -3.0,
+            -4.0,
+            -6.0,
+        ],
+        dtype=torch.float32,
+        device=code.device,
+    )
+    return lut[code.long()]
+
+
+def quantize_nvfp4_k_cache_into_reference(
+    k_nope: torch.Tensor,
+    k_rope: torch.Tensor,
+    kv_buffer: torch.Tensor,
+    loc: torch.Tensor,
+    global_scale: torch.Tensor | Real,
+) -> None:
+    """Bit-exact PyTorch reference for the mixed DSA row writer."""
+
+    k_nope, k_rope, rows, loc = _validate_quant_inputs(k_nope, k_rope, kv_buffer, loc)
+    if loc.numel() == 0:
+        return
+    g = _as_global_scale(global_scale, rows.device)
+    blocks = _sanitize_nonfinite_torch(k_nope.float(), g).reshape(
+        -1, _NUM_LATENT_BLOCKS, NVFP4_BLOCK_SIZE
+    )
+    scale = (blocks.abs().amax(-1) / (_E2M1_MAX * g)).clamp(0, _E4M3_MAX)
+    scale_fp8 = scale.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    denominator = scale_fp8.float().unsqueeze(-1) * g
+    codes = _e2m1_rne_scaled_torch(blocks, denominator).reshape(-1, NVFP4_LATENT_DIM)
+    packed = codes[:, 0::2] | (codes[:, 1::2] << 4)
+    rope = torch.nan_to_num(
+        k_rope.float(),
+        nan=0.0,
+        posinf=torch.finfo(torch.bfloat16).max,
+        neginf=torch.finfo(torch.bfloat16).min,
+    )
+    rope_bytes = rope.to(torch.bfloat16).contiguous().view(torch.uint8)
+
+    valid = (loc >= 0) & (loc < rows.shape[0])
+    if not bool(valid.any()):
+        return
+    dst = loc[valid].long()
+    rows[dst, :NVFP4_PACKED_LATENT_BYTES] = packed[valid]
+    rows[
+        dst,
+        NVFP4_PACKED_LATENT_BYTES : NVFP4_PACKED_LATENT_BYTES + NVFP4_SCALE_BYTES,
+    ] = scale_fp8[valid].contiguous().view(torch.uint8)
+    rows[dst, -NVFP4_ROPE_BYTES:] = rope_bytes[valid]
+
+
+def dequantize_nvfp4_k_cache_paged_reference(
+    kv_buffer: torch.Tensor,
+    indices: torch.Tensor,
+    global_scale: torch.Tensor | Real,
+    dtype: torch.dtype = torch.bfloat16,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Gather and decode rows using the exact stored bytes as the reference."""
+
+    allowed = (torch.bfloat16, torch.float16, torch.float32, torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    if dtype not in allowed:
+        raise ValueError(f"unsupported output dtype: {dtype}")
+    rows = _as_cache_rows(kv_buffer)
+    indices = indices.reshape(-1)
+    if indices.dtype not in (torch.int32, torch.int64):
+        raise TypeError("indices must be int32 or int64")
+    if indices.device != rows.device:
+        raise ValueError("indices and cache must be on one device")
+    output = torch.zeros(
+        (indices.numel(), 1, NVFP4_LATENT_DIM + NVFP4_ROPE_DIM),
+        dtype=dtype,
+        device=rows.device,
+    )
+    if indices.numel() == 0:
+        return output
+    valid = (indices >= 0) & (indices < rows.shape[0])
+    if not bool(valid.any()):
+        return output
+    selected = rows[indices[valid].long()]
+    packed = selected[:, :NVFP4_PACKED_LATENT_BYTES]
+    codes = torch.empty(
+        (selected.shape[0], NVFP4_LATENT_DIM), dtype=torch.uint8, device=rows.device
+    )
+    codes[:, 0::2] = packed & 0x0F
+    codes[:, 1::2] = packed >> 4
+    scales = (
+        selected[
+            :,
+            NVFP4_PACKED_LATENT_BYTES : NVFP4_PACKED_LATENT_BYTES + NVFP4_SCALE_BYTES,
+        ]
+        .contiguous()
+        .view(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+        .float()
+    )
+    g = _as_global_scale(global_scale, rows.device)
+    latent = (
+        _decode_e2m1_torch(codes).reshape(-1, _NUM_LATENT_BLOCKS, NVFP4_BLOCK_SIZE)
+        * scales.unsqueeze(-1)
+        * g
+    ).reshape(-1, NVFP4_LATENT_DIM)
+    rope = selected[:, -NVFP4_ROPE_BYTES:].contiguous().view(torch.bfloat16)
+    output[valid, 0, :NVFP4_LATENT_DIM] = latent.to(dtype)
+    output[valid, 0, NVFP4_LATENT_DIM:] = rope.to(dtype)
+    return output
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _e2m1_rne_scaled_triton(x, denominator):
+    magnitude = tl.abs(x)
+    code = (
+        (magnitude > denominator * 0.25).to(tl.uint8)
+        + (magnitude >= denominator * 0.75).to(tl.uint8)
+        + (magnitude > denominator * 1.25).to(tl.uint8)
+        + (magnitude >= denominator * 1.75).to(tl.uint8)
+        + (magnitude > denominator * 2.5).to(tl.uint8)
+        + (magnitude >= denominator * 3.5).to(tl.uint8)
+        + (magnitude > denominator * 5.0).to(tl.uint8)
+    )
+    sign = ((x.to(tl.uint32, bitcast=True) >> 31).to(tl.uint8)) << 3
+    return tl.where(denominator > 0, code | sign, 0).to(tl.uint8)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _decode_e2m1_triton(code):
+    magnitude_code = code & 0x07
+    magnitude = tl.where(
+        magnitude_code == 0,
+        0.0,
+        tl.where(
+            magnitude_code == 1,
+            0.5,
+            tl.where(
+                magnitude_code == 2,
+                1.0,
+                tl.where(
+                    magnitude_code == 3,
+                    1.5,
+                    tl.where(
+                        magnitude_code == 4,
+                        2.0,
+                        tl.where(
+                            magnitude_code == 5,
+                            3.0,
+                            tl.where(magnitude_code == 6, 4.0, 6.0),
+                        ),
+                    ),
+                ),
+            ),
+        ),
+    )
+    return tl.where((code & 0x08) != 0, -magnitude, magnitude)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _quantize_nvfp4_k_cache_into_kernel(
+    k_nope_ptr,
+    k_rope_ptr,
+    rows_ptr,
+    loc_ptr,
+    global_scale_ptr,
+    num_rows,
+    k_nope_stride: tl.constexpr,
+    k_rope_stride: tl.constexpr,
+    row_stride: tl.constexpr,
+    NUM_LATENT_BLOCKS: tl.constexpr,
+    PACKED_BYTES: tl.constexpr,
+    SCALE_BYTES: tl.constexpr,
+    ROPE_DIM: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCKS_PER_PROGRAM: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    token = tl.program_id(0)
+    part = tl.program_id(1)
+    dst = tl.load(loc_ptr + token).to(tl.int64)
+    valid_dst = (dst >= 0) & (dst < num_rows)
+    safe_dst = tl.where(valid_dst, dst, 0)
+    g = tl.load(global_scale_ptr).to(tl.float32)
+
+    block = part * BLOCKS_PER_PROGRAM + tl.arange(0, BLOCKS_PER_PROGRAM)
+    lane = tl.arange(0, 16)
+    valid_block = block < NUM_LATENT_BLOCKS
+    offsets = block[:, None] * 16 + lane[None, :]
+    x = tl.load(
+        k_nope_ptr + token * k_nope_stride + offsets,
+        mask=valid_dst & valid_block[:, None],
+        other=0.0,
+    ).to(tl.float32)
+    # E2M1FN has no non-finite encoding: NaN -> +0, Inf -> recipe maximum.
+    bound = 6.0 * 448.0 * g
+    x = tl.where(
+        x != x,  # noqa: PLR0124  # Triton NaN test
+        0.0,
+        tl.maximum(tl.minimum(x, bound), -bound),
+    )
+    scale = tl.clamp(tl.max(tl.abs(x), axis=1) / (6.0 * g), 0.0, 448.0)
+    scale_fp8 = scale.to(tl.float8e4nv)
+    denominator = tl.expand_dims(scale_fp8.to(tl.float32) * g, 1)
+    codes = _e2m1_rne_scaled_triton(x, denominator)
+    pairs = tl.reshape(codes, (BLOCKS_PER_PROGRAM, 8, 2))
+    low, high = tl.split(pairs)
+    byte = tl.arange(0, 8)
+    tl.store(
+        rows_ptr + safe_dst * row_stride + block[:, None] * 8 + byte[None, :],
+        low | (high << 4),
+        mask=valid_dst & valid_block[:, None],
+    )
+    tl.store(
+        rows_ptr + safe_dst * row_stride + PACKED_BYTES + block,
+        scale_fp8.to(tl.uint8, bitcast=True),
+        mask=valid_dst & valid_block,
+    )
+
+    if part == tl.cdiv(NUM_LATENT_BLOCKS, BLOCKS_PER_PROGRAM) - 1:
+        rope_offset = tl.arange(0, ROPE_DIM)
+        rope = tl.load(
+            k_rope_ptr + token * k_rope_stride + rope_offset,
+            mask=valid_dst,
+            other=0.0,
+        ).to(tl.float32)
+        rope = tl.where(
+            rope != rope,  # noqa: PLR0124  # Triton NaN test
+            0.0,
+            tl.maximum(tl.minimum(rope, 3.3895313892515355e38), -3.3895313892515355e38),
+        ).to(tl.bfloat16)
+        rope_bits = rope.to(tl.uint16, bitcast=True)
+        tl.store(
+            rows_ptr
+            + safe_dst * row_stride
+            + PACKED_BYTES
+            + SCALE_BYTES
+            + 2 * rope_offset,
+            rope_bits & 0xFF,
+            mask=valid_dst,
+        )
+        tl.store(
+            rows_ptr
+            + safe_dst * row_stride
+            + PACKED_BYTES
+            + SCALE_BYTES
+            + 2 * rope_offset
+            + 1,
+            rope_bits >> 8,
+            mask=valid_dst,
+        )
+
+
+def quantize_nvfp4_k_cache_into(
+    k_nope: torch.Tensor,
+    k_rope: torch.Tensor,
+    kv_buffer: torch.Tensor,
+    loc: torch.Tensor,
+    global_scale: torch.Tensor | Real,
+) -> None:
+    """Quantize and scatter DSA keys into the 416-byte mixed cache rows."""
+
+    k_nope, k_rope, rows, loc = _validate_quant_inputs(k_nope, k_rope, kv_buffer, loc)
+    if loc.numel() == 0:
+        return
+    scale = _as_global_scale(global_scale, rows.device)
+    if not rows.is_cuda:
+        quantize_nvfp4_k_cache_into_reference(k_nope, k_rope, rows, loc, scale)
+        return
+    blocks_per_program = 8 if loc.numel() <= _QUANTIZE_SMALL_BATCH_THRESHOLD else 32

+    parts = triton.cdiv(_NUM_LATENT_BLOCKS, blocks_per_program)
+    _quantize_nvfp4_k_cache_into_kernel[(loc.numel(), parts)](
+        k_nope,
+        k_rope,
+        rows,
+        loc,
+        scale,
+        rows.shape[0],
+        k_nope.stride(0),
+        k_rope.stride(0),

+"""Measure NVFP4 pool writes, indexer transfer, and prefix materialization."""
+
+import argparse
+import gc
+import json
+import os
+import statistics
+import time
+from pathlib import Path
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import torch
+import torch.multiprocessing as mp
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def worker(rank, world, output, repeats):
+    os.environ["MASTER_ADDR"] = "127.0.0.1"
+    os.environ["MASTER_PORT"] = str(29830 + world)
+    os.environ["RANK"] = str(rank)
+    os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"] = str(rank)
+    os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"] = str(world)
+    torch.cuda.set_device(rank)
+
+    from sglang.srt.distributed.parallel_state import (
+        init_distributed_environment,

+    )

+    from sglang.srt.mem_cache.memory_pool import DSATokenToKVPool
+    from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_parallel
+
+    torch.manual_seed(42)
+    init_distributed_environment(
+        world_size=world,
+        rank=rank,
+        local_rank=rank,
+        distributed_init_method=f"tcp://127.0.0.1:{29830 + world}",
+        backend="nccl",
+    )
+    initialize_model_parallel(
+        tensor_model_parallel_size=world, attention_context_model_parallel_size=world
+    )
+    device = f"cuda:{rank}"
+    records = []
+    layers = [SimpleNamespace(layer_id=i) for i in range(78)]
+    loc = torch.arange(4096, device=device)
+    nope = torch.randn(4096, 1, 512, device=device).bfloat16()
+    rope = torch.randn(4096, 1, 64, device=device).bfloat16()
+    index = torch.ones(4096, 128, device=device).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    scale = torch.ones(4096, 1, device=device)
+
+    for capacity in (32768, 131072):
+        for mode in ("baseline", "layer_split_sync", "layer_split_prefetch"):
+            kwargs = dict(
+                size=capacity,
+                page_size=64,
+                dtype=torch.float4_e2m1fn_x2,
+                kv_lora_rank=512,
+                qk_rope_head_dim=64,
+                layer_num=78,
+                device=device,
+                index_head_dim=128,
+                enable_memory_saver=False,
+                kv_cache_dim=416,
+            )
+            if mode == "baseline":
+                pool = DSATokenToKVPool(**kwargs)
+            else:
+                pool = LayerSplitDSATokenToKVPool(
+                    **kwargs, layer_shard_rank=rank, layer_shard_size=world
+                )
+            for layer in layers:
+                pool.set_mla_kv_global_scale(layer.layer_id, 0.5 + layer.layer_id / 128)
+            sizes = [None] * world
+            torch.distributed.all_gather_object(
+                sizes,
+                int(pool.get_kv_size_bytes()),
+                group=get_parallel().attn_cp_group.cpu_group,
+            )
+
+            def step(current_pool):
+                for layer in layers:
+                    if mode == "layer_split_prefetch":
+                        current_pool.prefetch_kv_buffer(layer.layer_id)
+                    current_pool.set_mla_kv_buffer(layer, loc, nope, rope)
+                    current_pool.index_key_cache.store_quantized(
+                        layer.layer_id, loc, index, scale
+                    )
+                    current_pool.index_key_cache.get_buffer(layer.layer_id)
+                    current_pool.get_mla_kv_buffer(layer, loc)
+
+            # These are kernel warmups. No model or dataset is loaded.
+            step(pool)
+            step(pool)
+            samples = []
+            for _ in range(3):
+                torch.cuda.synchronize()
+                torch.distributed.barrier()
+                start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+                end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+                wall_start = time.perf_counter()

+                end.record()
+                end.synchronize()
+                times = torch.tensor(
+                    [
+                        start.elapsed_time(end) / repeats,
+                        1000 * (time.perf_counter() - wall_start) / repeats,
+                    ],
+                    device=device,

+                samples.append(times.tolist())
+            records.append(

+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", required=True, type=Path)
+    parser.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=20)

+    if torch.cuda.device_count() < 4:

+    args.output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

+        mp.spawn(
+            worker, args=(world, str(output), args.repeats), nprocs=world, join=True
+        )

+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+r"""Compare full-layer and active-page NVFP4 prefill transfers on 2/4 GPUs.
+
+Run inside an existing allocation (this script never requests GPUs)::
+
+    python scripts/bench_dsa_nvfp4_prefill_pages.py \
+        --world-sizes 2 4 --pool-pages 256 4096 65536 --active-pages 64 \
+        --near-full-fraction 0.9 --output prefill-pages.json
+
+Every mode reads the same pages. The ordinary NVFP4 pool is the correctness
+reference. Timed steps include CPU page planning, metadata communication,
+packing, broadcast, scatter, index gathering, NVFP4 dequantization, the real
+H64 FlashMLA sparse-prefill consumer, and final device synchronization.
+Initialization, correctness checks, and the inter-rank start barrier are not
+timed. This is a local transfer/consumer benchmark, not model throughput.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import gc
+import hashlib
+import importlib.metadata
+import importlib.util
+import json
+import math
+import os
+import socket
+import statistics
+import subprocess
+import time
+from datetime import UTC, datetime
+from pathlib import Path
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import torch
+import torch.multiprocessing as mp
+
+PAGE_SIZE = 64
+KV_ROW_BYTES = 416
+INDEX_ROW_BYTES = 132
+MODES = ("full_sync", "full_prefetch", "partial_prefetch")
+
+
+def _write_json(path: Path, data: dict) -> None:
+    temporary = path.with_suffix(path.suffix + ".tmp")
+    temporary.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2, allow_nan=False) + "\n")
+    temporary.replace(path)
+
+
+def _command(argv: list[str], cwd: Path | None = None) -> str | None:
+    try:
+        result = subprocess.run(
+            argv, cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False
+        )
+    except FileNotFoundError:
+        return None
+    return result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else None
+
+
+def _source_identity() -> dict:
+    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+    files = [
+        "scripts/bench_dsa_nvfp4_prefill_pages.py",
+        "python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/dsa_cache_layer_split.py",
+        "python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py",
+        "python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa/nvfp4_k_cache.py",
+        "python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa_backend.py",
+        "python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa/dsa_indexer.py",
+        "python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa/utils.py",
+        "python/sglang/srt/model_executor/pool_configurator.py",
+        "python/sglang/kernels/ops/kvcache/dsa_index_k_cache.py",
+    ]
+    git_diff = _command(["git", "diff", "HEAD", "--", *files], root)
+    versions = {}
+    for package in ("torch", "sglang", "sglang-kernel", "triton", "flashinfer-python"):
+        try:
+            versions[package] = importlib.metadata.version(package)
+        except importlib.metadata.PackageNotFoundError:
+            versions[package] = None
+    native_module = importlib.util.find_spec("sgl_kernel.flashmla_ops")
+    native_path = (
+        Path(native_module.origin) if native_module and native_module.origin else None
+    )
+    return {
+        "git_head": _command(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], root),
+        "source_commit_env": os.environ.get("SOURCE_COMMIT"),
+        "tracked_diff_sha256": (
+            hashlib.sha256(git_diff.encode()).hexdigest()
+            if git_diff is not None
+            else None
+        ),
+        "file_sha256": {
+            name: hashlib.sha256((root / name).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
+            for name in files
+        },
+        "versions": versions,
+        "flashmla_native": (
+            {
+                "path": str(native_path),
+                "sha256": hashlib.sha256(native_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
+            }
+            if native_path is not None and native_path.is_file()
+            else None
+        ),
+        "torch_cuda": torch.version.cuda,
+        "slurm_job_id": os.environ.get("SLURM_JOB_ID"),
+    }
+
+
+def _summary(values: list[float]) -> dict:
+    ordered = sorted(values)
+
+    def quantile(fraction: float) -> float:
+        position = fraction * (len(ordered) - 1)
+        lower = math.floor(position)
+        upper = math.ceil(position)
+        return ordered[lower] + (ordered[upper] - ordered[lower]) * (position - lower)
+
+    return {
+        "median": statistics.median(values),
+        "mean": statistics.mean(values),
+        "p10": quantile(0.1),
+        "p90": quantile(0.9),
+        "max": max(values),
+        "stdev": statistics.stdev(values) if len(values) > 1 else 0.0,
+    }
+
+
+def _metadata(pool_pages: int, active_pages: int, world: int, rank: int, args):
+    device = f"cuda:{rank}"
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(args.seed + pool_pages + active_pages)
+    pages_cpu = torch.randperm(pool_pages, generator=generator)[:active_pages] + 1
+    # Production DSA metadata uses int32 physical page tables. Keep that dtype
+    # here so the benchmark exercises the same gather address arithmetic.
+    pages = pages_cpu.to(device=device, dtype=torch.int32)
+    slots = (
+        pages[:, None] * PAGE_SIZE + torch.arange(PAGE_SIZE, device=device)
+    ).flatten()
+    rows_per_request = args.pages_per_request * PAGE_SIZE
+    requests = math.ceil(active_pages / args.pages_per_request)
+    lengths_cpu = torch.tensor(
+        [
+            min(rows_per_request, slots.numel() - i * rows_per_request)
+            for i in range(requests)
+        ],
+        dtype=torch.int32,
+    )
+    table = torch.zeros((requests, rows_per_request), dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    table.flatten()[: slots.numel()] = slots.to(torch.int32)
+    ends = lengths_cpu.to(torch.int64).cumsum(0).to(device=device) - 1
+    reference_slots = torch.arange(PAGE_SIZE, PAGE_SIZE + slots.numel(), device=device)
+    reference_pages = torch.arange(
+        1, active_pages + 1, device=device, dtype=torch.int32
+    )
+    query_count = max(16, math.ceil(requests / world))
+    request_ids = (rank + torch.arange(query_count, device=device) * world) % requests
+    lengths = lengths_cpu.to(device=device)
+    query_lengths = lengths[request_ids].clamp(max=2048)
+    relative = torch.arange(2048, device=device)
+    indices = request_ids[:, None] * rows_per_request + relative
+    indices = torch.where(relative < query_lengths[:, None], indices, -1)
+    query_generator = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(args.seed + rank)
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        pages=pages,
+        pages_cpu=pages_cpu,
+        slots=slots,
+        full_page_table=table,
+        seq_lens_cpu=lengths_cpu,
+        extend_seq_lens_cpu=[1] * requests,
+        out_cache_loc=slots[ends],
+        # The consumer gathers the same flattened batch on every rank.
+        consumer_lens=torch.tensor([slots.numel()], device=device, dtype=torch.int32),
+        reference_slots=reference_slots,
+        reference_pages=reference_pages,
+        q=torch.randn(
+            query_count,
+            64,
+            576,
+            generator=query_generator,
+            device=device,
+            dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        ),
+        topk=indices.to(torch.int32).unsqueeze(1).contiguous(),
+        topk_length=query_lengths.to(torch.int32),
+        requests=requests,
+    )
+
+
+def _initialize(pool, reference, meta, layers: int, args) -> None:
+    """Use the unchanged production writer for both physical page layouts."""
+    for layer_id in range(layers):
+        layer = SimpleNamespace(layer_id=layer_id)
+        global_scale = 0.5 + layer_id * 0.375
+        pool.set_mla_kv_global_scale(layer_id, global_scale)
+        reference.set_mla_kv_global_scale(layer_id, global_scale)
+        generator = torch.Generator(device=pool.device).manual_seed(
+            args.seed + layer_id
+        )
+        for start in range(0, meta.slots.numel(), 16384):
+            stop = min(start + 16384, meta.slots.numel())
+            count = stop - start
+            nope = torch.randn(
+                count,
+                1,
+                512,
+                generator=generator,
+                device=pool.device,
+                dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+            )
+            rope = torch.randn(
+                count,
+                1,
+                64,
+                generator=generator,
+                device=pool.device,
+                dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+            )
+            index_keys = torch.randn(
+                count, 128, generator=generator, device=pool.device
+            ).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+            index_scales = (
+                torch.rand(count, 1, generator=generator, device=pool.device) + 0.25
+            )
+            for current, slots in (
+                (pool, meta.slots[start:stop]),
+                (reference, meta.reference_slots[start:stop]),
+            ):
+                current.set_mla_kv_buffer(layer, slots, nope, rope)
+                current.index_key_cache.store_quantized(
+                    layer_id, slots, index_keys, index_scales
+                )
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+
+def _begin(pool, meta, mode: str) -> None:
+    if mode == "partial_prefetch":
+        pool.begin_prefill_page_plan(
+            meta.full_page_table,
+            meta.seq_lens_cpu,
+            meta.extend_seq_lens_cpu,
+            meta.out_cache_loc,
+        )
+    else:
+        pool.clear_prefill_page_plan()
+
+
+def _read_and_consume(pool, meta, layer_id: int, mode: str):
+    from sgl_kernel.flash_mla import flash_mla_sparse_fwd
+    from sglang.kernels.ops.kvcache import dsa_index_k_cache
+    from sglang.srt.layers.attention.dsa.nvfp4_k_cache import (
+        dequantize_nvfp4_k_cache_paged,
+    )
+
+    if mode == "reference":
+        index_buffer = pool.index_key_cache.get_buffer(layer_id)
+        pages, slots = meta.reference_pages, meta.reference_slots
+    elif mode == "partial_prefetch":
+        pool.index_key_cache.prepare_prefill_buffer(layer_id)
+        index_buffer = pool.index_key_cache.get_prefill_buffer(layer_id)
+        pages, slots = meta.pages, meta.slots
+    else:
+        index_buffer = pool.index_key_cache.get_buffer(layer_id)
+        if mode == "full_prefetch":
+            pool.prefetch_kv_buffer(layer_id)
+        pages, slots = meta.pages, meta.slots
+
+    # This production index gather can overlap the async main-KV transfer.
+    index_keys, index_scales = dsa_index_k_cache.GetKAndS.execute(
+        pool,
+        index_buffer,
+        page_indices=pages.view(1, -1),
+        seq_len_tensor=meta.consumer_lens,
+        seq_len_sum=slots.numel(),
+        max_seq_len=slots.numel(),
+    )
+    raw = (
+        pool.get_prefill_key_buffer(layer_id)
+        if mode == "partial_prefetch"
+        else pool.get_key_buffer(layer_id)
+    )
+    decoded = dequantize_nvfp4_k_cache_paged(
+        raw, slots, pool.get_mla_kv_global_scale(layer_id), dtype=torch.bfloat16
+    )
+    attention = flash_mla_sparse_fwd(
+        q=meta.q,
+        kv=decoded,
+        indices=meta.topk,
+        sm_scale=576**-0.5,
+        d_v=512,
+        topk_length=meta.topk_length,
+    )[0]
+    return raw, index_buffer, index_keys, index_scales, decoded, attention
+
+
+def _check(pool, reference, meta, layers: int, mode: str) -> None:
+    _begin(pool, meta, mode)
+    # A prior full transfer must not hide a missing page in the partial path.
+    pool.remote_kv_buffer.fill_(0xA5)
+    pool.index_key_cache.remote_buffer.fill_(0x5A)
+    if mode == "partial_prefetch":
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            pool.prefill_page_ids[: pool.prefill_num_pages],
+            meta.pages.sort().values.to(torch.int64),
+            rtol=0,
+            atol=0,
+        )
+    for layer_id in range(layers):
+        actual = _read_and_consume(pool, meta, layer_id, mode)
+        expected = _read_and_consume(reference, meta, layer_id, "reference")
+        # Check every consumed packed page, including all FP8 index scale bytes.
+        for start in range(0, meta.pages.numel(), 1024):
+            pages = meta.pages[start : start + 1024]
+            reference_pages = meta.reference_pages[start : start + 1024]
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                actual[0].view(-1, PAGE_SIZE * KV_ROW_BYTES)[pages],
+                expected[0].view(-1, PAGE_SIZE * KV_ROW_BYTES)[reference_pages],
+                rtol=0,
+                atol=0,
+            )
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                actual[1][pages], expected[1][reference_pages], rtol=0, atol=0
+            )
+        for got, wanted in zip(actual[2:5], expected[2:5]):
+            torch.testing.assert_close(got, wanted, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        # Retain the existing native NVFP4 attention tolerance.
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual[5], expected[5], atol=8e-4, rtol=2.01 / 128)
+        del actual, expected
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+
+def _step(pool, meta, layers: int, mode: str) -> float:
+    plan_start = time.perf_counter()
+    _begin(pool, meta, mode)
+    plan_ms = (time.perf_counter() - plan_start) * 1000
+    for layer_id in range(layers):
+        result = _read_and_consume(pool, meta, layer_id, mode)
+        del result
+    return plan_ms
+
+
+def _time_step(pool, meta, layers: int, mode: str) -> dict:
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    torch.distributed.barrier()
+    start, end = (
+        torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True),
+        torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True),
+    )
+    wall_start = time.perf_counter()
+    start.record()
+    plan_ms = _step(pool, meta, layers, mode)
+    end.record()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    return {
+        "wall_ms": (time.perf_counter() - wall_start) * 1000,
+        "cuda_elapsed_ms": start.elapsed_time(end),
+        "plan_host_ms": plan_ms,
+    }
+
+
+def _byte_counts(
+    pool_pages: int, active_pages: int, layers: int, world: int, mode: str
+):
+    pages = active_pages if mode == "partial_prefetch" else pool_pages + 1
+    main = pages * PAGE_SIZE * KV_ROW_BYTES * layers
+    index = pages * PAGE_SIZE * INDEX_ROW_BYTES * layers
+    plan_ids = active_pages * 8 if mode == "partial_prefetch" else 0
+    return {
+        "main_kv_broadcast_payload_bytes": main,
+        "index_broadcast_payload_bytes": index,
+        "plan_id_broadcast_payload_bytes": plan_ids,
+        "broadcast_payload_bytes": main + index + plan_ids,
+        "logical_receiver_bytes": (main + index + plan_ids) * (world - 1),
+        "main_bytes_consumed_per_rank": active_pages
+        * PAGE_SIZE
+        * KV_ROW_BYTES
+        * layers,
+        "index_bytes_consumed_per_rank": active_pages
+        * PAGE_SIZE
+        * INDEX_ROW_BYTES
+        * layers,
+        "note": "Payload sizes exclude NCCL protocol and small plan-object framing; logical receiver bytes are not measured fabric traffic.",
+    }
+

+        )

+            )

+    Its scales and the next page are entirely above the boundary. Two unequal
+    requests also check the flattened output offsets without a large output.
+    """

+    page_bytes = page_size * (head_dim + 4)
+    boundary_page = (2**31) // page_bytes
+    pool = SimpleNamespace(
+        index_page_size=page_size, index_head_dim=head_dim, quant_block_size=head_dim
+    )
+    buf = torch.empty((boundary_page + 2, page_bytes), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+    # Keep the page table and writer input in the int32 metadata format used by
+    # the runtime. Only four pages need initialization in this >2 GiB buffer.
+    pages = torch.tensor(
+        [[boundary_page + 1, 0], [boundary_page - 1, boundary_page]],
+        dtype=torch.int32,
+        device="cuda",
+    )
+    loc = (
+        pages.flatten()[:, None] * page_size
+        + torch.arange(page_size, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")

+@torch.inference_mode()
+def _run_nvfp4_owner_graph_case(rank: int, world: int, query_count: int, mode):
+    """An eager prefix changes scratch state between graph replays.
+
+    The next decode must use the new owner-local KV and index bytes. This
+    protects the non-PD owner route from stale scratch tags, capture-time
+    tensor values, and a broadcast whose root differs from layer ownership.
+    """
+    from sgl_kernel import flashmla_nvfp4_ops, flashmla_ops  # noqa: F401
+    from sglang.srt.layers.attention.dsa_backend import DeepseekSparseAttnBackend
+    from sglang.srt.mem_cache.dsa_cache_layer_split import LayerSplitDSATokenToKVPool
+    from sglang.srt.mem_cache.memory_pool import DSATokenToKVPool
+    from sglang.srt.model_executor.forward_batch_info import ForwardMode
+
+    device = f"cuda:{rank}"
+    kwargs = {
+        "size": SIZE,
+        "page_size": PAGE_SIZE,
+        "kv_lora_rank": KV_LORA_RANK,
+        "dtype": torch.float4_e2m1fn_x2,
+        "qk_rope_head_dim": QK_ROPE,
+        "layer_num": 5,
+        "device": device,
+        "index_head_dim": INDEX_HEAD_DIM,
+        "enable_memory_saver": False,
+        "kv_cache_dim": 416,
+    }
+    reference = DSATokenToKVPool(**kwargs)
+    pool = LayerSplitDSATokenToKVPool(
+        **kwargs,
+        layer_shard_rank=rank,
+        layer_shard_size=world,
+        unified_decode=True,
+    )
+    assert pool.use_owner_compute(mode)
+    assert not pool.use_owner_compute(ForwardMode.EXTEND)
+    generator = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(9100 + query_count)
+    layers = [
+        SimpleNamespace(
+            layer_id=layer_id, head_dim=576, v_head_dim=512, tp_q_head_num=64
+        )
+        for layer_id in range(5)
+    ]
+    backend = SimpleNamespace(token_to_kv_pool=pool)
+    for layer in layers:
+        for current in (reference, pool):
+            current.set_mla_kv_global_scale(layer.layer_id, 0.5 + layer.layer_id / 4)
+
+    loc = torch.arange(65, 65 + query_count, device=device)
+    nope = torch.empty(5, query_count, 1, 512, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    rope = torch.empty(5, query_count, 1, 64, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    index_keys = torch.empty(
+        5, query_count, 128, device=device, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn
+    )
+    index_scales = torch.empty(5, query_count, 1, device=device)
+    q = torch.empty(5, query_count, 1, 64, 576, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    index_q = torch.empty(5, query_count, 128, device=device)
+    valid = torch.zeros(SIZE + PAGE_SIZE, device=device, dtype=torch.bool)
+    valid[1:65] = True
+    metadata, num_splits = torch.ops.sgl_kernel.get_mla_decoding_metadata.default(
+        torch.ones(query_count, device=device, dtype=torch.int32),
+        64,
+        1,
+        64,
+        True,
+        2048,
+    )
+
+    def random_values(count):
+        return (
+            torch.randn(count, 1, 512, device=device, generator=generator).bfloat16(),
+            torch.randn(count, 1, 64, device=device, generator=generator).bfloat16(),
+            torch.randn(count, 128, device=device, generator=generator).to(
+                torch.float8_e4m3fn
+            ),
+            torch.rand(count, 1, device=device, generator=generator) + 0.5,
+        )
+
+    def prefill_write(write_loc):
+        for layer in layers:
+            values = random_values(write_loc.numel())
+            for current in (reference, pool):
+                current.set_mla_kv_buffer(layer, write_loc, values[0], values[1])
+                current.index_key_cache.store_quantized(
+                    layer.layer_id, write_loc, values[2], values[3]
+                )
+        # Leave the eager scratch tagged layer 0, unlike the graph's final
+        # layer 4. The production forward boundary must invalidate it.
+        # Enter the real partial-plan boundary after an owner graph replay.
+        # Page zero used by the legacy codec fixture is not a request page.
+        table = torch.arange(64, 128, device=device).view(1, -1)
+        pool.begin_prefill_page_plan(
+            table, torch.tensor([64]), [1], table[:, -1:].flatten()
+        )
+        pool.prefetch_prefill_kv_buffer(0)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            pool.get_prefill_key_buffer(0)[64:128],
+            reference.get_key_buffer(0)[64:128],
+            rtol=0,
+            atol=0,
+        )
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            pool.index_key_cache.get_prefill_buffer(0)[1],
+            reference.index_key_cache.get_buffer(0)[1],
+            rtol=0,
+            atol=0,
+        )
+
+    def fill_step(step):
+        loc.copy_(torch.arange(query_count, device=device) + 65 + step * query_count)
+        valid[loc] = True
+        for layer in layers:
+            layer_id = layer.layer_id
+            values = random_values(query_count)
+            nope[layer_id].copy_(values[0])
+            rope[layer_id].copy_(values[1])
+            index_keys[layer_id].copy_(values[2])
+            index_scales[layer_id].copy_(values[3])
+        q.copy_(torch.randn(q.shape, device=device, generator=generator).bfloat16())
+        index_q.copy_(torch.randn(index_q.shape, device=device, generator=generator))
+
+    def select_indices(current, layer_id):
+        # Independently unpack the production page layout. This small
+        # indexer uses 16 candidates so changing the stored K/scales changes
+        # the selected tokens. Transport still uses the native 2048 width.
+        raw = (
+            current.get_owned_index_buffer(layer_id)
+            if current is pool
+            else current.index_key_cache.get_buffer(layer_id)
+        )
+        keys = raw[:, : PAGE_SIZE * 128].reshape(-1, 128)
+        keys = keys.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn).float()
+        scales = raw[:, PAGE_SIZE * 128 :].contiguous().view(torch.float32)
+        keys = keys * scales.reshape(-1, 1)
+        logits = index_q[layer_id] @ keys.T
+        logits.masked_fill_(~valid.unsqueeze(0), -torch.inf)
+        selected = torch.topk(logits, 16, dim=-1).indices.to(torch.int32)
+        indices = torch.full((query_count, 2048), -1, device=device, dtype=torch.int32)
+        indices[:, :16] = selected
+        return indices
+
+    def decode(current, layer_id, indices):
+        packed = (
+            current.get_owned_key_buffer(layer_id)
+            if current is pool
+            else current.get_key_buffer(layer_id)
+        )
+        return torch.ops.sgl_kernel.sparse_decode_fwd_nvfp4.default(
+            q[layer_id],
+            packed.view(-1, 64, 1, 416),
+            current.get_mla_kv_global_scale(layer_id),
+            indices.unsqueeze(1),
+            None,
+            None,
+            metadata,
+            num_splits,
+            512,
+            576**-0.5,
+        )[0]
+
+    def forward(current):
+        result = []
+        for layer in layers:
+            layer_id = layer.layer_id
+            if current is pool:
+                current.run_on_layer_owner(
+                    layer_id,
+                    lambda layer=layer, layer_id=layer_id: (
+                        current.set_owned_mla_kv_buffer(
+                            layer, loc, nope[layer_id], rope[layer_id]
+                        )
+                    ),
+                    shape=None,
+                    dtype=torch.uint8,
+                    device=device,
+                )
+            else:
+                current.set_mla_kv_buffer(layer, loc, nope[layer_id], rope[layer_id])
+            current.index_key_cache.store_quantized(
+                layer_id, loc, index_keys[layer_id], index_scales[layer_id]
+            )
+            if current is pool:
+                indices = current.run_on_layer_owner(
+                    layer_id,
+                    lambda layer_id=layer_id: select_indices(current, layer_id),
+                    shape=(query_count, 2048),
+                    dtype=torch.int32,
+                    device=device,
+                )
+                output = DeepseekSparseAttnBackend._forward_on_layer_owner(
+                    backend,
+                    q[layer_id],
+                    None,
+                    layer,
+                    lambda layer_id=layer_id, indices=indices: decode(
+                        current, layer_id, indices
+                    ),
+                )
+            else:
+                indices = select_indices(current, layer_id)
+                output = decode(current, layer_id, indices)
+            # If the helper reuses a result buffer, keep each layer's own
+            # output before the next layer broadcasts into that buffer.
+            result.append((indices.clone(), output.clone()))
+        return result
+
+    prefill_write(torch.arange(1, 65, device=device))
+    fill_step(0)
+    warmup_stream = torch.cuda.Stream(device=device)
+    warmup_stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+    with torch.cuda.stream(warmup_stream):
+        for _ in range(2):
+            pool.prepare_owner_compute()
+            forward(pool)
+            forward(reference)
+    torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(warmup_stream)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    torch.distributed.barrier()
+    pool.prepare_owner_compute()
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        captured = forward(pool)
+
+    for step in range(4):
+        # Interleave a prefill-like mutation and scratch materialization
+        # before every replay, including an existing prefix token.
+        prefill_write(torch.tensor([31 + step], device=device))
+        fill_step(step)
+        pool.prepare_owner_compute()
+        graph.replay()
+        expected = forward(reference)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        for layer_id, (actual_pair, expected_pair) in enumerate(
+            zip(captured, expected)
+        ):
+            torch.testing.assert_close(actual_pair[0], expected_pair[0], rtol=0, atol=0)
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                actual_pair[1], expected_pair[1], atol=8e-4, rtol=2.01 / 128
+            )
+            if pool._is_layer_owned(layer_id):
+                assert torch.equal(
+                    pool.get_owned_key_buffer(layer_id),
+                    reference.get_key_buffer(layer_id),
+                )
+                assert torch.equal(
+                    pool.get_owned_index_buffer(layer_id),
+                    reference.index_key_cache.get_buffer(layer_id),
+                )
+        # Eager reads after graph execution must also materialize the
+        # current owner bytes rather than reuse a capture-time scratch tag.
+        pool.prepare_owner_compute()
+        for layer in layers:
+            assert torch.equal(
+                pool.get_key_buffer(layer.layer_id),
+                reference.get_key_buffer(layer.layer_id),
+            )
+            assert torch.equal(
+                pool.index_key_cache.get_buffer(layer.layer_id),
+                reference.index_key_cache.get_buffer(layer.layer_id),
+            )
+    torch.distributed.barrier()
+    print(
+        f"[rank {rank}] NVFP4 owner graph CP={world} Q={query_count}: "
+        "four replays, eager prefixes, index/KV bytes and native outputs OK",
+        flush=True,
+    )
+
+
+def _run_nvfp4_owner_graph(rank: int, world: int):
+    from sglang.srt.model_executor.forward_batch_info import ForwardMode
+
+    for query_count, mode in ((1, ForwardMode.DECODE), (6, ForwardMode.TARGET_VERIFY)):
+        _run_nvfp4_owner_graph_case(rank, world, query_count, mode)
